findings.title: Create passes original unmutated object to Legacy.Create instead of the created object
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` is called first and returns `created` (which has generated fields populated, such as `Name` when `GenerateName` is used, `UID`, `ResourceVersion`, and `CreationTimestamp`), while `d.Legacy.Create` is then called in a goroutine with the original `obj` (or if `Storage.Create` mutates `obj` in place, reading/mutating the same pointer concurrently with the caller returning `created` and serializing it is a data race). When `GenerateName` is used (as tested in `playlist_test.go`), `Legacy.Create` will either generate a different name/UID than unified storage or fail/race on shared state.

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive context from the HTTP request context, causing cancellation as soon as the handler returns
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine creates its timeout context from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Once the synchronous `d.Storage.*` call completes and the method returns to the HTTP handler, the HTTP server cancels the request `ctx` as soon as the response is written. This will immediately cancel the in-flight or not-yet-scheduled `d.Legacy.*` operation in the background goroutine instead of giving it the intended 10s timeout. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` should be used before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Wrong metric recorded in Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection
findings.body:
Several metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record the wrong metric or label:
- Line 45 (`Create` error path): calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration` when `d.Storage.Create` fails.
- Line 106 (`Delete` success path): passes `name` (the object name, which is unbounded cardinality) instead of `options.Kind` as the `kind` argument to `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 129 (`Update` error path): calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration` when `d.Storage.Update` fails.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection` async legacy path): calls `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration` for the `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` call.

findings.title: Unit tests share a non-thread-safe testify mock.Mock with background goroutines
findings.body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `mock.Mock` instance, and `DualWriterMode3` invokes `d.Legacy.*` in a background goroutine without any synchronization before the test returns. Moreover, in `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` (and the error cases of `Create`/`Update` where `setupStorageFn` is nil), expectations are not even set up for both calls or `m.On` matches the wrong store. When the background goroutine runs concurrently with test completion or subsequent calls on `m`, `testify/mock` will either race on `m.Calls` or panic with an unexpected method call (e.g., `Delete` is only mocked once, or `Legacy.Delete` is called with no expectation or races).
